subject: Citrine model onboarding: compatibility edge-case, pin request & rollout timing
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Rebecca Chen <rchen@kata.ai>
Cc: onboarding@kata.ai
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Citrine model onboarding: compatibility edge-case, pin request & rollout timing

Hey team — looping you all on Citrine-7B-v2-quant (vendor: Kata AI). Product had a successful eval for our latency/cost targets, but the model has two integration quirks I want ops/infra and eng to validate before we let it loose in staging. High-level ask: can we provisionally pin this variant for a 3-week integration window (pin to v2-quant) while we complete compatibility checks and a canary? If we see regressions, we want an automatic fallback to Citrine-7B-v1 (existing variant).

What we know so far:
- Model name: Citrine-7B-v2-quant (ops note: quantized INT8 release)
- Primary concerns: tokenizer/vocab rearrangement (vocab indices shifted), and a small change to KV cache ordering that may break warm-caching across model variants.
- Business ask: Product needs a firm go/no-go within 48 hours so we can commit to the customer pilot next quarter.

Attachments: citrine-7b-v2-integration-checklist.pdf (initial artifacts from Kata).

Specific asks by team:
- Dev/Infra (Dev Patel + Jonas): quick compatibility triage (tokenizer mapping, KV cache compatibility, memory profile) and an estimate for a staging run.
- Platform/Release (Marissa + Karthik): preferred canary window and telemetry hooks we must enable to detect regressions for semantic quality and latency.
- Evals (Priyom): any additional eval sets we should run that would be sensitive to tokenizer index shifts (tokenization edge cases, prompt truncation tests).

Rebecca — if there are sample vocab files or a migration guide from Kata, please attach. If procurement/PO timing affects rollout, flag it here (cc: onboarding).

I want a short status update in ~24 hours and a firm recommendation in 48. If we move forward, I will request a temporary variant pin (3 weeks) and coordinate the fallback mapping. Thanks.

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior PM, Model Platform
Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Rebecca Chen <rchen@kata.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 17:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Citrine model onboarding: compatibility edge-case, pin request & rollout timing

Lauren — quick tech note after an initial look at the artifacts.

Summary:
- Tokenizer: looks like Kata moved from a 50k BPE vocabulary to a 49,120-piece SentencePiece-like vocab. Index remapping is NOT 1:1; there are shifted indices for ~3k tokens (primarily punctuation clusters and some compound tokens). That will break any cached token-id assumptions in upstream tokenizers unless we map explicitly.
- KV cache: the new runtime writes KV planes with a different layout (channels transposed for performance on their runtime). We can transform at inference runtime but there is ~2–4ms extra per call for the conversion when warm cache is used (cost impact, but acceptable for canary).
- Memory: quantized INT8 reduces footprint ~30% but peak activation patterns differ slightly; need a staging run with typical 512-token prompts to validate batch packing heuristics.

Attachments: tokenizer-lookup-diff.patch (I attached a small script that produces a remap table — not production-ready).

Next steps I propose:
1) Ops: run a quick staging job with a 1000-request sample (mixed prompt lengths) and capture tokenization failures, memory & tail latency. I can spin up a sandbox GPU pool for this.
2) Platform: enable a KV-conversion path behind a toggle; if we pin the variant, the conversion toggle should default on for the pinned window.
3) Evals: Priyom, please prioritize tokenization-sensitive evals (truncation, edge punctuation, multilingual snippet tests).

I can have an initial staging run and report within ~18 hours if we get the sample set and a short canary plan.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Citrine model onboarding: compatibility edge-case, pin request & rollout timing

Thanks — quick ops perspective. I'm OK with a provisional 3-week pin but we have to lock the canary window and telemetry before we flip anything. My recommendations:

- Canary window: 72 hours with progressive traffic (1%, 5%, 20%) if staging passes. We should enforce a hard rollback at the 20% milestone if semantic quality drops on any monitored prompt family.
- Telemetry: enable token-level latency histograms, top-50 prompt regression alerts (Priyom to define), and automatic rollback triggers if p95 latency increases >30% or error rate >0.5%.
- Capacity: schedule the staging run outside the monthly maintenance window — ops can run Wednesday 23rd (UTC) with a small dedicated GPU pool.

I attached a short canary-plan.md that covers toggles, rollback gates, and who to notify. If Dev can provide the KV-conversion toggle by EOD tomorrow, I can wire the rollout and add the fallback to v1 in the routing table.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Platform Release Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Citrine model onboarding: compatibility edge-case, pin request & rollout timing

Hi Lauren / team — thanks for the quick review and for flagging the tokenizer/KV notes. A few items from Kata's side:

- We pushed an internal migration guide and the vocab files to the attachment you received. The vocab reorder is regrettable (it came from a pre-release optimization) but we can provide a remap table and a thin compatibility shim if needed. I'll attach the remap and an engineer from our side can jump into a short sync.
- SOC2 / compliance: our SOC2 report is attached to the onboarding portal; if you need a signed addendum for the pilot, let me know — procurement typically needs ~10 business days for an addendum.
- POC: I'm assigning Daniel Park (daniel.park@kata.ai) as our integration engineer; he'll be cc'd on follow-ups and can join the staging run if you want vendor-side telemetry.

We are fine with a provisional 3-week pin and fallback to v1; thank you for the suggested gates. Let us know if you want us to deliver remap tooling earlier (we can prioritize).

— Rebecca Chen
Head of Platform Partnerships
Kata AI

Subject: Re: Citrine model onboarding: compatibility edge-case, pin request & rollout timing

Thanks everyone — good progress. Quick summary and owners so we can move to action: 

Decisions:
- Approve provisional variant pin for Citrine-7B-v2-quant for 3 weeks, conditional on staging run passing tokenization + memory checks and the canary gates Marissa outlined.
- Fallback: automatic routing to Citrine-7B-v1 if rollback triggers fire.

Owners & next steps:
- Dev Patel: run the 1k-request staging job (sandbox GPU pool) and deliver tokenization failure report + KV-conversion toggle by EOD tomorrow. Attachments: use tokenizer-lookup-diff.patch as a starting point.
- Priyom Das: queue tokenization-sensitive evals and provide the top-20 prompt families to monitor.
- Marissa Cole: schedule canary on Wed 23rd (UTC) and wire telemetry/rollback gates (canary-plan.md attached).
- Rebecca / Kata: please share the remap table and have Daniel Park standby for the staging window. Procurement note accepted — if an addendum is required, procurement should start ASAP.

I'll open a Jira (PROD-2143) and update the intake with pin metadata and the fallback routing configuration. If anyone sees a blocker (procurement, SOC2, or critical staging failures) flag it in the Jira and ping me immediately.

Thanks — I'll follow up with the Jira link and a short sync invite for Monday.

— Lauren

Redwood Inference
